messages.subject: NYSE holiday before 1971
messages.body_plain:
Hello

Thanks for writing and maintaining the Rmetrics package!

I am working with the Rmetrics holiday calendar and noticed a slight 
error in NYSE holidays before 1971.
I have to admit my point to be picky (who cares about trading holiday's 
before 1971), but you might still want to correct the source code.

According to NYSE's holiday calendar,  Washington's birthay was observed 
at NYSE as follows:
http://www.nyse.com/about/newsevents/1176373643795.html:[..] * 
Washington's Birthday was first declared a federal holiday by an 1879 
act of Congress. The Monday Holiday Law, enacted in 1968, shifted the 
date of the commemoration of Washington's Birthday from February 22 to 
the third Monday in February [..]
http://www.nyse.com/pdfs/closings.pdf [..] Washington's Birthday (Feb. 
22) Closed every year. Observed on Mondays since 1971.[..]

The function holidayNYSE implements WashingtonsBirthday/PresidentsDay by 
calling USWashingtonsBirthday() before 1971 and USPresidentsDay() from 
1971 on.
Unfortunately, USWashingtonsBirthday() is defined in the same way as 
USPresidentsDay() (third Monday in February) instead of returning 
February 22nd.
    USWashingtonsBirthday <- function (year = currentYear)
    {
        # instead of the third Monday in February (ans = 
.nth.of.nday(year, 2, 1, 3))
        # use February 22nd as trading holiday on NYSE before 1971
        ans = year * 10000 + 222
        timeDate(as.character(ans))
    }

Please also note a slight error in the holidayNYSE function: the 
following conditions are both TRUE for the year 1970. The second 
condition should read (y > 1970) instead of (y >= 1970).
    holidayNSYE <- function( year=currentYear )
    [..]
        if (y <= 1970)
            holidays = c(holidays, as.character(USWashingtonsBirthday(y)))
        if (y >= 1970)
            holidays = c(holidays, as.character(USPresidentsDay(y)))
    [..]


Best Regards,
Lukas Elmiger

messages.subject: fGarch: possible bug(s)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

In the summary function of fGarch, I would suggest that standardised residuals are computed as:

r.s = object at residuals/object at sigma.t

because r.s = object at residuals/sqrt(object at h.t) is wrong for aparch models, in which it does not hold that sigma = h^(1/2). The correct expression that holds in general is: sigma = h^(1/delta).

In fGarch 260.72 sigma.t is calculated as: (.series$h)^deltainv, where deltainv = 1/fit$params$delta. However, fit$params$delta does not get updated with coefficient estimates and thus is always equal to 2. This leads to wrong calculation of sigma.t, which is always equal to h^(1/2).
Has this problem been solved in the development version of Rmetrics (fGarch)?

Thanks for your answer.

Best regards

Michal Miklovic

Hi,

I would like to ask if was possible to implement in a function computing gradient in the fGarch package. Or is there a quick and easy way of implementing a gradient function so that I can do it myself? Based on the paper 'Parameter Estimation of ARMA Models with GARCH/APARCH Errors' by Wuertz, Chalabi and Luksan, I think that a function computing gradient was available for garch models in Rmetrics in the past. The reason for my question is that I would like to calculate robust covariance matrix (and robust standard errors) for a garch model estimated under the assumption of normally distributed standardised errors, for which I need hessian and gradient. The robust covariance matrix for such a QML estimator is computed as hessian^(-1)*OPG*hessian^(-1), where OPG is the outer product of the gradient, i.e. gradient*(transposed gradient). Clearly, hessian is available but I do not have the gradient.
Maybe the robust covariance matrix could be implemented at some point in the future along the following lines:

## robust works only for cond.dist == norm
if (cov.matrix == "robust") {
fit$cvar = solve(fit$hessian) %*% (gradient %o% gradient) %*% solve(fit$hessian)
} else {
fit$cvar = solve(fit$hessian) }


Thanks for your answer.

Best regards

Michal Miklovic

Hi Yohan,

Not offense meant - sorry if that came across as such.  Rmetrics is
the gold standard when it comes to breadth and overall usefulness.
Always appreciative of you and your team's efforts.

The purpose of my comment was with respect to using timeDate as an
indexing class.  I'll clarify to the list with a more clear response,
but I think my reasoning is that even the primary timeSeries class
doesn't utilize timeDate for its @positions/charvec.  That coupled
with what seemed like a situation that could be handled with something
simpler in POSIXct was the _why_.

That said, timeDate as a tool seems great.  I have yet to fully grasp
its power (or place in a workflow), but I none-the-less interested in
it.  If you look at 'xts' you can see that one can easily allow an
'xts' object to use 'timeDate' for indexing.  [ indexClass(x) <-
'timeDate' ]

I have been meaning to email you about a few things with respect to my
'xts' package and 'timeSeries'/'timeDate':

A quick primer on 'xts':

Basically enforces a time-based
(Date,POSIXct,chron,timeDate,yearmon,yearqtr) index in a modified
'zoo' class, while allowing for arbitrary attributes to be appended
(like time zone, data source, comments...).  The latter is only unique
in that these attributes are displayed differently by using xts as
opposed to zoo.  In zoo and other classes, they just clutter up the
screen.  I like the additional features of timeSeries quite a bit -
but in reality the S4 object just doesn't work in many functions that
aren't built for it.

The main usefulness for developers is in the conversion scheme.
'as.xts' allows for lossless conversion of one object into 'xts', and
'reclass()' reverses the procedure.  Basically the parts of the
original object that need to be remembered for re-conversion are
assigned to xtsAttributes.

Inside functions it is possible to simply 'as.xts' the time-series
input (can be of any class: timeSeries, ts, zoo, its, irts, even
properly formed (rownames in suitable date-convertible format) matrix

messages.subject_clean: fGarch: possible bug(s) in ICS & LLH in summary
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I wanted to compare several garch models on the basis of information criteria statistics (ICS) and I found a possible bug, which affects a couple of computations in fGarch.

First, I would suggest that the log likelihood in the summary function is reported as follows:

LLH = (-1)*object at fit$value

because it should be the value of maximised log likelihood (and not minimised negative log likelihood). The consequent discrepancy with the iteration path output could be solved by printing the following:

cat("\nFinal Estimate of the Negative LLH:\n")


Second, I would suggest changing the hessian and covariance matrices calculations to, respectively:

fit$hessian = (-1)*.garch??DAHessian( ... )

fit$cvar = (-1)*solve(fit$hessian)

These changes would have no effect on the estimates of covariance matrix (and thus also standard errors) but the hessian matrix would correspond to a maximised log likelihood, which is currently not the case, and would have negative numbers on the diagonal, which is rather intuitive for a maximum.


Finally, I would suggest removing the minus sign from the computation of the ICS since (-2)*(-1)*fit$value = 2*fit$value = 2*LLH(as defined above, i.e. maximised log likelihood). I think the ICS should be computed from the maximised value of the (log) likelihood function (and not from minimised negative (log) likelihood). Tsay (2002) in Analysis of Financial Time Series states that, in AIC calculation, "the likelihood function is evaluated at the maximum likelihood estimates".

Best regards,

Michal Miklovic
